title: CCATT to the Rescue w/Slate
description: Critical situations call for critical thinking. Airman First Class Thomas Barley introduces us to team kadena's Critical Care Transport Team whose quick thinking is saving lives.

transcript.text: - [A1C Barley] In dire situations,
^cooperation and partnership can be the difference
^between life and death.
On Kadena, Navy and Air Force personnel
worked together to gather equipment
that will help transfer a 16-month old burn victim
from mainland Japan to a burn hospital in California.
- We are using equipment
that's never before flown on a C-17.
^We looked at everything else in the inventory
^and all of our other options
^and realized it wasn't going to work for the patient.
Normally when you're transporting small infants
who you're worried about thermal regulation,
whether you can keep them warm,
whether you can keep the ambient humidity up.
This patient's a little older, greater than a year old.
So, he wasn't going to fit in any of those options.
- [A1C Barley] And when you're out of options,
who better to ask for help but family.
Personnel had to think outside the box
and reach out to their sister services.
- Not only do we have multiple units coming together
to figure out a safe plan to transport this patient
but we have multiple services as well.
We wouldn't be able to take this piece of equipment
if the U.S. Naval Hospital on Okinawa
wasn't willing to release it to us for the mission.
So we have not only multiple units
but fairly joint service to make this happen.
- [A1C Barley] Working together,
Air Force and Navy personnel were able
to lead the way in innovation,
accomplish the mission,
and change the way future missions are carried out.
Airman First Class Thomas Barley,
Kadena Air Base, Japan.
